findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} lists 201 response, not 200
findings.evidence: responses: "201": {"description":"Success", schema PhysicalCard}; no 200 response is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 unless the server really returns 201 for a GET.

findings.title: Vault GET and POST responses lack error or 404 documentation
findings.evidence: Only 200 and 400 are declared; the 400 uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse, and no 401, 403, or 404 is listed. Compare POST /reimbursements/mileage, which declares 401 but no 400.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 401, 403 and 404 (and 400 for POST /cards/vault) consistently across all endpoints.

findings.title: Many write and read endpoints declare no error responses
findings.location: PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; POST /developer/v1/cards/physical; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements/{reimbursement_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}
findings.evidence: PATCH physical card has only a 200 response. GET virtual card has only a 200 response. GET reimbursement and GET reimbursements have only 200. PATCH transaction has only 200. Some endpoints document 400 and others do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a documented 400/401/403/404 response using DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical 400 response is an untyped string
findings.evidence: "400": {"description":"Error", "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"type":"string"}}}}
findings.suggested_fix: Return the DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema, as other endpoints do, so the error body is typed.

findings.title: Mileage POST and receipt upload use different auth and error patterns
findings.evidence: "security": [] (no auth) on a write endpoint while all other operations require oauth2 scopes; it documents only a 401 response.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override or explain it, and add the required reimbursements:write scope.

findings.title: Vault POST security scope differs from its sibling endpoints
findings.evidence: security: cards:read_vault and limits:write, while the GET /cards/vault/{card_id} uses only cards:read_vault. The operation both creates a limit and returns PAN/CVV.
findings.suggested_fix: Document why both scopes are needed and state in the description what sensitive data the response returns.

findings.title: Idempotency key is optional on create but not on receipt upload
findings.evidence: Vault POST has header X-Idempotency-Key with required: false. Receipt upload has body field idempotency_key listed in required, but the same concept is a header elsewhere. POST /cards/physical and POST /reimbursements/mileage have no idempotency key at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header or body) with consistent required status across all create endpoints.

findings.title: Receipt upload path and parameter names are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Path uses singular 'reimbursement' while other paths use 'reimbursements'. Body field 'reimbursee_id' is used here while the mileage body uses the same 'reimbursee_id', and list endpoints use 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the path to /reimbursements/submit-receipt and document how reimbursee_id differs from user_id.

findings.title: Transaction listing mixes casing in query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards uses 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'. Transactions uses 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id and order_by_amount_asc, keeping snake_case throughout.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor and page_size limits are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Virtual cards: page_size has default 20 but no min/max constraint in schema. Reimbursements and transactions say 'must be between 2 and 100'. Physical cards list has no pagination parameters at all, yet returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same page_size and start parameters, with the same min/max constraints, to every paginated list endpoint.

findings.title: Physical card list endpoint has no paging parameters
findings.evidence: Operation id is 'get_physical_card_list_with_pagination' and the response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource, but parameters include only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters, or remove 'pagination' from the operation id and response if it is not paginated.

findings.title: Transaction list returns counts that the other lists lack
findings.evidence: Response is CountedPaginatedResponseApiTransactionCanonicalSchema with include_count described as 'total_count, capped at 10,000'. Other list endpoints return DeveloperAPINestedPage with no total_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the other list endpoints that total counts are unavailable, or add them consistently.

findings.title: Transaction amount field is deprecated but still typed as number
findings.evidence: Transaction: "amount": {"deprecated":true, "type":"number"}; SingleTransaction: "amount": {"deprecated":true, "type":"string"}. Same field, different types.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for amount in both schemas, or remove the field from SingleTransaction.

findings.title: Transaction SingleTransaction and Transaction amount/currency types conflict
findings.evidence: Transaction.original_transaction_amount uses CurrencyAmount (amount, currency_code), while merchant_amount uses ApiSignedAmount (currency, value). Both describe the same kind of money with different field names.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one money shape (for example ApiSignedAmount) across transaction and reimbursement schemas, or document the difference.

findings.title: Reimbursement schema marks many nullable fields as required with no nullability reason
findings.evidence: required includes 'payment_id', 'payment_batch_id', 'approved_at', 'distance', 'end_location', 'merchant' and 'employee_id', all declared nullable: true. Also 'waypoints' and 'trace_id' are not required in some places.
findings.suggested_fix: Document when each nullable required field is null, or make optional fields non-required.

findings.title: Card vault PAN and CVV returned with no declared protection
findings.evidence: CardDetails has pan: "Primary account number(PAN) of the card." and cvv: "Card verfication value." with no security note; GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id} declares only oauth2 cards:read_vault and no x-sensitive or equivalent marker. PhysicalCard.shipping.full_card_number is also a plain string.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark PAN/CVV as sensitive (e.g. x-sensitive: true, writeOnly/no-cache headers), document the protection, and add Cache-Control: no-store to the response.

findings.title: Full card number exposed in shipping object without protection
findings.evidence: "full_card_number":{"type":"string","description":"The full card number."} is part of CardShipping, returned by GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} (scope cards:read, not cards:read_vault).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from CardShipping or gate it behind cards:read_vault with the same sensitive-field marking as CardDetails.

findings.title: Card-creation and vault endpoints lack declared idempotency on writes
findings.evidence: POST /developer/v1/cards/vault defines optional header X-Idempotency-Key, but POST /developer/v1/cards/physical and POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage declare no idempotency mechanism; /reimbursement/submit-receipt uses a body field idempotency_key instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism (header, required on creates) consistently across all POST create endpoints.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security requirements
findings.evidence: "security":[] with no scope, and the only error response is 401; a creation endpoint that moves money has no declared oauth2 scope (reimbursements:write expected).
findings.suggested_fix: Declare security: [{oauth2: [reimbursements:write]}] matching the other reimbursement write endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card POST returns plain-string 400 error body
findings.evidence: "400":{"description":"Error","content":{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"string"}}}} whereas all other 400 responses use DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use $ref DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response and add x-trace-id header as elsewhere.

findings.title: Many error and success responses lack x-trace-id or error schema
findings.evidence: PATCH physical card declares only 200; GET virtual card only 200; GET vault card has 400 but PATCH transaction only 200; no DeveloperApiErrorResponse documented for these operations.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 400/401/404 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse and x-trace-id on every operation.

findings.title: Pagination parameter naming inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual (userId, start); GET /developer/v1/cards/physical (user_id); GET /developer/v1/transactions (orderByAmountAsc vs order_by_amount_desc)
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is "userId" while all others use "user_id"; transactions has "orderByAmountAsc" alongside snake_case "order_by_amount_desc" and "order_by_date_asc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and keep one convention for all query parameters.

findings.title: Pagination start cursor and page_size limits not enforced in schema
findings.evidence: page_size is "type":"integer","default":20 with description "must be between 2 and 100" but no minimum/maximum; start is an unconstrained string. Physical card list has no page_size or start parameter at all despite returning a paginated response.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2, maximum: 100 to page_size and add start/page_size to the physical card list, or document why not.

findings.title: Physical card list parameters conflict with description and naming
findings.evidence: Description says cards "can be filtered by ... display name" and the parameter is display_name, but include_activated_only says "Defaults to True if not specified" and no default is in schema; include_terminated_only defaults are only in prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Put defaults in the schema (default: true / false) so the type and description agree, and align filter names with the response field names.

findings.title: Transaction amount types conflict with description
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is "type":"number" (float) while SingleTransaction.amount is "type":"string", both marked deprecated; min_amount/max_amount accept decimal string or number via oneOf.
findings.suggested_fix: Make amount type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction and document precision; prefer string decimals or integer minor units throughout.

findings.title: Reimbursement state filter and transaction state enum inconsistent
findings.evidence: Transaction state enum includes "ALL" as a state value, which is a query sentinel not a valid stored state; the response schema for state therefore allows a value that never occurs.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove ALL from the response state enum and keep it only as a request filter value.

findings.title: Reimbursement user identifier named inconsistently
findings.evidence: Query param user_id has no description and is declared last among parameters; create body uses reimbursee_id for the same concept (POST /reimbursements/mileage and submit-receipt).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name for the reimbursement owner concept across list filters and create bodies, and describe user_id.

findings.title: Operation summary contradicts method for virtual card GET
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation, returning a VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and verify no delete operation was intended.

findings.title: Split transaction PATCH is destructive yet lacks safety docs
findings.evidence: Operation has "x-destructive":true and an empty line_items array 'unsplit (remove all line items)' but no idempotency or concurrency guidance, and tags include both "Transaction" and "transactions" (case-variant duplicate tag).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate 'transactions' tag and document the replace semantics and how to retry safely.

findings.title: Transaction amount fields lack unit and sign clarity
findings.evidence: "amount": {"deprecated": true, "description": "Deprecated. Use `entity_amount`.", "type": "number"} in Transaction, but typed as "type": "string" in SingleTransaction. Same field, different types across list and single endpoints; no unit stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one type (string decimal or number) for amount in both schemas and state the currency and unit explicitly, or remove the field before sunset.

findings.title: Currency amount units inconsistent across endpoints
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmount.amount: "expressed in cents"; ApiSignedAmount.value: "smallest denomination"; ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody.amount: "Amount in minor units (e.g. 5000 = $50.00)"; ApiSpendingRestrictionsRequestBody.limit: "denominated in the smallest currency unit"; transaction-level "amount" is a plain decimal number. Multiple money representations with no single rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one money type (integer minor units plus currency and minor_unit_conversion_rate) everywhere and document it once.

findings.title: Request money amounts have no range or minimum
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmountRequestBody: "amount": {"type": "integer"} with no minimum, and no note on whether negative or zero is allowed. ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody: "amount": {"type": "integer"} with no minimum. By contrast ApiReimbursementAmount.value has "minimum": 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare minimum (and whether negatives are valid) on every amount input, and state the maximum allowed.

findings.title: Currency code is free string despite enum elsewhere
findings.evidence: "currency_code": {"default": "USD", "description": "The type of currency, in ISO 4217 format. e.g. USD for US dollars", "type": "string"} with no enum, while ApiSignedAmount.currency and ApiReimbursementAmount.currency carry a full enum. Also CurrencyAmount requires minor_unit_conversion_rate but the request type does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same ISO 4217 enum to all currency fields and document which currencies are supported for limits.

findings.title: Timestamps without format on several fields
findings.evidence: Reimbursement examples use "created_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" (malformed, missing hour), and ApiTransactionPurchaseLodging.check_in is "type": "string" with no format; ApiTransactionPurchaseFlightData.departure_date is "type": "string", nullable, no format.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare format: date or date-time on every date field and fix the malformed example timestamps.

findings.title: Date filter formats and time zones undefined
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements params from_date, to_date, from_submitted_at, to_transaction_date; GET /developer/v1/transactions from_date, to_date
findings.evidence: Parameter "to_transaction_date" description is just "Data."; "from_transaction_date" says "after this date" with format date-time, while transactions "from_date" says "ISO8601 format" with no timezone rule. Inclusive vs exclusive boundaries are not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the time zone (UTC expected), inclusive/exclusive semantics, and replace "Data." with a real description.

findings.title: Enum for reimbursement state missing from transaction filters and pagination limits incomplete
findings.evidence: Reimbursement and transaction page_size: "The value must be between 2 and 100." but the schema is only "default": 20, "type": "integer" with no minimum or maximum. Virtual cards page_size has the same default with no bounds; its description is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2 and maximum: 100 to every page_size schema, and state behavior when out of range.

findings.title: Pagination cursor type and meaning unspecified
findings.evidence: "start": {"type": "string"} described as "The ID of the last entity of the previous page", yet GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual and physical list use a different scheme with no start parameter at all, and physical cards list has no page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the cursor's opaque nature, and add consistent pagination params (page_size, start) across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination controls
findings.evidence: Parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only, yet the response is a PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a next URL. No start or page_size is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size with bounds, or document the fixed page size and how to reach later pages.

findings.title: Default for include_activated_only contradicts parameter semantics
findings.evidence: "Filter only for activated cards. Defaults to True if not specified" with no schema default; and include_terminated_only "Defaults to False" also undeclared in schema. Defaults live only in prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare default values in the schema so client generators and docs agree.

findings.title: Reimbursement sync and funding fields have undocumented enum values
findings.evidence: funding_source enum includes "RAMP_FUNDED" with description "RAMP_FUNDED does not confirm settlement", while trace_id is described as "may be a trace ID, IMAD number, or reference number" with descriptor/trace_id both nullable and no format, so consumers cannot parse it reliably.
findings.suggested_fix: Document which rails return which trace types and define nullability and format precisely.

findings.title: Reimbursement pagination uses undocumented user_id param and inconsistent naming
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements param user_id and userId on GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual
findings.evidence: Reimbursements has "user_id" with no description; virtual cards list uses "userId" (camelCase) while every other filter is snake_case, e.g. "entity_id" and "is_terminated".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and add descriptions to every query param.

findings.title: Trip and transaction state enums incomplete for state filter
findings.evidence: Filter enum includes "ALL" and "DECLINED" but Transaction.state enum is identical; the description says "If state is not set, all transactions except declined transactions will be returned" with no statement of what the response state value will be when declined.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether declined transactions can appear in responses and document the ALL value's semantics.

findings.title: Responses lack error schema on several endpoints and 201 vs 200 inconsistency
findings.evidence: get_physical_card_resource returns "201" for success, while the other GETs return 200. POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400 returns "type": "string" instead of DeveloperApiErrorResponse. Many operations (e.g. PATCH physical card, POST mileage) declare no 400/404 at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for GET, use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all 4xx, and document error codes for each operation.

findings.title: Idempotency key defined inconsistently across creation endpoints
findings.location: POST /developer/v1/cards/vault header X-Idempotency-Key vs POST /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt body idempotency_key
findings.evidence: Vault creation: header "X-Idempotency-Key", optional, maxLength 255. Receipt upload: body field "idempotency_key" is required with no length limit. Other creates (physical card POST, mileage POST) have no idempotency mechanism at all, and the physical card POST can create cards that cost money.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize one optional-or-required idempotency key mechanism with defined retention window across all POST endpoints, starting with card creation.

findings.title: Approval states and statuses lack meaning and next steps
findings.evidence: Enum values such as 'PENDING' ('Pending Review'), 'APPROVED' ('Approved'), 'AWAITING_PAYMENT' ('Awaiting Payment'), 'EXPORTED' ('Exported for payment'), 'INIT' ('Init') and 'DRAFT' ('Draft') have only short labels. Nothing says which states are final, which precede approval, or which can move back.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description for each state explaining whether it is pending, approved, paid, or terminal, and what transitions are possible.

findings.title: Transaction approval_status values are undefined
findings.evidence: Enum: AWAITING_EMPLOYEE, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_CHANGES_REQUESTED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_MISSING_ITEMS, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_REPAYMENT_FAILED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_REPAYMENT_REQUESTED, AWAITING_REVIEWER, FULLY_APPROVED. No descriptions are provided, and the Transaction schema has no approval_status field to confirm the values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add x-enum-descriptions for each value and include approval_status in the Transaction response schema with the same definitions.

findings.title: Transaction 'state' enum mixes states and filter values
findings.evidence: Response state enum includes 'ALL', which is described as 'Special filter value to include all transaction states'. The description for state says only 'transaction state.' It is unclear whether 'COMPLETION' or 'PENDING_INITIATION' is final.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'ALL' from the response schema enum and define the lifecycle order of the remaining states.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'sync_status' and 'synced_at' semantics unclear
findings.evidence: sync_status enum NOT_SYNC_READY/SYNCED/SYNC_READY has descriptions, but 'synced_at' says 'Time when reimbursement has been synced. Will be None if...' while the field is nullable and no timezone is given. The 'sync_status' field is marked readOnly with no description.
findings.suggested_fix: State who or what triggers sync, what 'NOT_SYNC_READY' requires, and whether synced_at is in UTC.

findings.title: Amount fields are inconsistent and some lack units
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is 'type: number' and deprecated, while SingleTransaction.amount is 'type: string' with the same description 'Deprecated. Use entity_amount.' Neither says what currency or units it uses. Transaction.entity_amount is an integer in minor units, while merchant_amount is also signed without explaining which amount is what the business is charged.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the type of 'amount' identical in both schemas, and state the currency and minor-unit meaning of each amount field.

findings.title: Negative and signed amounts not explained for approvals
findings.evidence: ApiSignedAmount.value: 'May be negative for refunds or credits.' Transaction.entity_amount is described as 'signed: refunds and credits can be negative.' No guidance is given on how a negative amount affects approval thresholds or totals.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain how negative amounts are treated for approval, reporting, and split totals.

findings.title: Transaction split behavior and line-item sums undefined
findings.evidence: Description says 'the line item amounts must sum to the transaction amount', but does not say which amount (entity_amount, merchant_amount, or amount) or what happens on a mismatch. Operation is marked 'x-destructive': true, yet the description does not say what is overwritten.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the exact amount field used for the sum, document the error on mismatch, and state what previous splits or memos are replaced.

findings.title: No audit trail or who/when fields on approvals
findings.evidence: Transaction has 'updated_at' described only as 'Approximate transaction updated timestamp... Computed as the latest of user transaction time, settlement time, and transaction interaction state update time.' Reimbursement has 'updated_at' with no description. No field identifies who approved, rejected, or last changed a record.
findings.suggested_fix: Add approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, and last_modified_by fields, or explain how these are retrieved, with the timestamp source documented.

findings.title: Reimbursement dates have undefined meaning
findings.evidence: Query 'from_date' is 'Filter reimbursements created after this date' while 'from_transaction_date' is 'Filter by underlying transaction date (after this date)'. 'to_transaction_date' has the description 'Data.' Reimbursement.transaction_date is a 'date' with no definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Data.' with a real definition and state whether date filters are inclusive, and which timezone applies.

findings.title: Transaction date filter descriptions conflict
findings.evidence: from_date: 'with a user_transaction_time after the given date'. order_by_date_asc: 'Sort transactions by user_transaction_date...' which is a field name that does not exist in the Transaction schema (the field is user_transaction_time). 'accounting_date' is described separately as based on cleared date or manual override.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent date field name, and state which date (user_transaction_time, settlement_date, or accounting_date) each filter uses.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'spend_limit_id' versus 'fund_id' is unclear
findings.evidence: spend_limit_id is 'deprecated: true', described as 'Alias of fund_id (Fund).' Mileage create uses 'spend_allocation_id' described as 'Unique identifier of the fund', and the list endpoint has no fund filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name for the fund across request and response, and document the deprecation date and replacement.

findings.title: Physical card states and suspension reversibility unclear
findings.evidence: state enum: 'ACTIVE','CHIP_LOCKED','SUSPENDED','TERMINATED','UNACTIVATED'. Post suspension says 'The suspension is revertable.' but no reference to who may unsuspend. The DELETE for termination says only 'irreversible', and 'x-destructive' is absent from it.
findings.suggested_fix: State which actor can make each state change and what audit record is produced.

findings.title: Virtual card DELETE described as 'Permanently delete' but GET
findings.evidence: summary: 'Permanently delete this resource' on a GET operation, with a description of 'Get single virtual card'.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to describe fetching the card, and confirm whether any delete operation exists for virtual cards.

findings.title: Vault 'Create' response type mismatch
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' returns schema PCILimit, which has 'restrictions' and 'card' but no description of whether the request's 'accounting_rules' were applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Document whether the returned limit reflects the accounting_rules sent, and what the 'allowed_overage_percent_override' null means.

findings.title: Transaction 'card_holder' and attendee fields need source
findings.evidence: card_holder is 'Information about the card holder' with department_name and location_name but no note that these are copied at transaction time or live values. attendees: 'List of attendees for the transaction' with user_id that may be null.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether card_holder values are snapshots at the time of the transaction and when attendee user_id is null.

findings.title: Scopes not declared for vault create endpoint's card reads
findings.evidence: security: [{"oauth2":["cards:read_vault","limits:write"]}] - the operation requires both scopes together, but the summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' does not say both are needed, and it is unclear whether a token with only one scope gets partial results or a 403.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the description that both cards:read_vault and limits:write are required (AND semantics), and document the 401/403 response for a missing scope.

findings.title: Auth-failure responses undocumented on most operations
findings.location: All operations except POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage and POST /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt
findings.evidence: Only POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage and submit-receipt document 401; e.g. GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id} lists only 200 and 400 while requiring oauth2 cards:read_vault, and POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage has "security": [] while declaring a 401 response.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare 401 and 403 consistently on every secured operation, and fix the mileage endpoint's empty security array so its auth requirement is explicit.

findings.title: Mileage create endpoint has empty security requirement
findings.evidence: "security":[],"summary":"Create a mileage reimbursement" - no scope is named, yet the same operation returns 401 Unauthorized.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to oauth2 with reimbursements:write, or explain why no scope is needed.

findings.title: Summary of virtual card GET says 'Permanently delete'
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation whose description is absent and whose response is "Get single virtual card".
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and add a DELETE operation if deletion is intended.

findings.title: Physical card delete vs. terminate wording is ambiguous
findings.evidence: summary "Terminate a card", description "Please note that this action is irreversible."; the sibling POST /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}/suspension is described as "The suspension is revertable." and the unsuspend DELETE has no description.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent verbs and state explicitly in each description which action is reversible and which endpoint undoes it.

findings.title: Unsuspend and suspend operations use inconsistent verbs
findings.evidence: DELETE /suspension has summary "Unsuspend a card" with no description and no 400 response, while POST /suspension returns 400 and says "The suspension is revertable."
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description and 400 response to the DELETE, and make the suspend/unsuspend pair symmetric.

findings.title: Transaction list filters conflict with sync_status precedence
findings.evidence: sync_status: "If set, it supersedes sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits", while sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits remain separate parameters with no deprecation note.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits deprecated, or document the precedence in a single place.

findings.title: Date filters for transactions use different fields
findings.evidence: from_date "Filter for transactions with a user_transaction_time after..." and order_by_date_asc "Sort transactions by user_transaction_date" (a field name not in the Transaction schema); updated_after is not documented as to which timestamp.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same field name everywhere (user_transaction_time) and state which timestamp updated_after compares against.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination and sort parameter naming
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is "userId" while all other filters are snake_case user_id; transactions sort uses "orderByAmountAsc" alongside "order_by_amount_desc" and "order_by_date_asc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId and orderByAmountAsc to snake_case and add the missing order_by_amount_asc counterpart.

findings.title: Reimbursement filter 'data' description is meaningless
findings.evidence: "description":"Data." for to_transaction_date; similarly include_merchant_data and GET /transactions/{transaction_id} include_merchant_data use "Data."
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the filter (e.g. 'Filter transactions dated before this timestamp') and state what extra data include_merchant_data adds.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor semantics are unclear
findings.evidence: "start": "The ID of the last entity of the previous page..." with type string, while the response page.next is a full URL string with '<new_params>' placeholder; physical cards list has no start/page_size at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that the next URL should be used verbatim, and give physical card listing the same pagination parameters or state why it has none.

findings.title: Reimbursement submit-receipt idempotency is duplicated
findings.evidence: Request body has required "idempotency_key" while the vault creation endpoint uses header "X-Idempotency-Key" (optional); the receipt endpoint's 201 response does not say whether repeat calls return the same reimbursement.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism (header or body) across endpoints and document the replay behavior and response on a duplicate key.

findings.title: Receipt endpoint path differs from reimbursements resource
findings.evidence: Path uses singular "reimbursement/" while all other reimbursement paths use "reimbursements" (e.g. /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt, or keep the old path as a documented alias.

findings.title: Physical card POST response contract is unclear
findings.evidence: 400 response has "schema": {"type":"string"} while every other endpoint returns DeveloperApiErrorResponse; GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 201 instead of 200 for success.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 and return 200 for the GET success case.

findings.title: Transaction split fields reference unlisted ids and lookup keys
findings.evidence: Description says "Send line_items with amounts (in minor units)" but ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody.amount is an integer with no currency, and the transactions list returns entity_amount in value form; the patch 200 response does not define any error responses (no 400) despite the description requiring amounts to sum to the transaction amount.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 400 response with error codes for sum mismatch and document the currency of amount, and the required error response.

findings.title: No rate limit, retry, or backoff guidance anywhere in spec
findings.evidence: The spec has no description of rate limits, 429 responses, Retry-After headers, or retry guidance; no operation documents a 429 or 5xx response.
findings.suggested_fix: Document per-client rate limits, add 429 responses with Retry-After, and state which failures are safe to retry.

findings.title: Mutating POSTs lack idempotency keys
findings.evidence: Only POST /developer/v1/cards/vault defines X-Idempotency-Key as optional; create-physical-card and mileage-reimbursement have no idempotency input, and submit-receipt has a required idempotency_key in the body with no description of its retention window or conflict behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism consistently to all POST create operations and document key lifetime and replay behavior.

findings.title: Idempotency mechanism inconsistent between header and body
findings.evidence: Vault creation uses header 'X-Idempotency-Key' (optional, 1-255 chars), while receipt upload uses a required body field 'idempotency_key' with no length limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one transport (header) and one validation rule set for idempotency keys across all endpoints.

findings.title: Page size limits are documented inconsistently or missing
findings.evidence: Virtual cards, reimbursements, and transactions state 'must be between 2 and 100' for page_size, but physical cards list has no page_size or pagination parameters at all despite returning PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource.
findings.suggested_fix: Add page_size (min, max, default) and a cursor parameter to every paginated list, including physical cards.

findings.title: Pagination cursor semantics are unclear
findings.evidence: 'start' is described as 'The ID of the last entity of the previous page', typed as plain string, and page.next is a URL template '<resources>?<new_params>' with no example of a real next link.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to 'cursor' or document it as opaque, state whether next is absolute and how to detect the last page, and document ordering guarantees.

findings.title: Physical card list cannot be paginated or sorted
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource, yet the operation defines only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only with no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same start and page_size parameters used by the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Pagination and filter parameter names mix conventions
findings.evidence: Query params use camelCase 'userId' and 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside snake_case 'user_id', 'order_by_date_asc', and 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on snake_case for every query parameter and deprecate the camelCase names with an alias period.

findings.title: Inconsistent success status codes across operations
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 201; POST /developer/v1/cards/physical returns 200; DELETE /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 204
findings.evidence: GET '/developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}' responses lists '201': Success; POST '/developer/v1/cards/physical' lists '200': Success for creation.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads, 201 for creates, and 204 or 200 consistently for deletes, correcting the GET 201 response.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented or untyped on many operations
findings.location: POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400; PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage 401 only
findings.evidence: POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400 uses schema type 'string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH and several GET list operations define no error responses; reimbursement list has no 400 despite filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all 4xx and 5xx responses and document the error_code values per operation.

findings.title: Error descriptions are vague and not operation-specific
findings.evidence: Responses say 'raises CardInvalidInput' or 'raises TransactionInvalidInput', which are implementation exception names rather than client-facing descriptions; error_code values are never enumerated.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with client-facing descriptions and list the stable error_code values each operation can return.

findings.title: Ambiguous mixed-state transaction list default
findings.evidence: Description says 'If state is not set, all transactions except declined transactions will be returned', while the 'state' enum includes 'ALL' and the note on 'include_count' says counts add latency; no default is in the schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the default in the schema and state explicitly how 'ALL' differs from the unset default.

findings.title: Unclear and deprecated amount fields in transaction schema
findings.evidence: 'amount' is 'type: number' in Transaction but 'type: string' in SingleTransaction, and is marked deprecated; 'limit_id' is deprecated but still required-adjacent with 'fund_id' returning the same value.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix one type for amount across both schemas and set a removal date for deprecated fields.

findings.title: Patch semantics for transaction split are unclear and destructive
findings.evidence: Marked 'x-destructive': true; description says 'Send an empty line_items array to unsplit' and line_items 'Omit to leave splits unchanged', with no statement on whether repeated calls are safe or what happens on partial failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replacement semantics, retry safety, and the conflict response when amounts do not sum to the transaction amount.

findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} lists 201 response, not 200
findings.evidence: responses: "201": {"description":"Success", schema PhysicalCard}; no 200 response is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200 unless the server really returns 201 for a GET.

findings.title: Vault GET and POST responses lack error or 404 documentation
findings.evidence: Only 200 and 400 are declared; the 400 uses DeveloperApiErrorResponse, and no 401, 403, or 404 is listed. Compare POST /reimbursements/mileage, which declares 401 but no 400.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 401, 403 and 404 (and 400 for POST /cards/vault) consistently across all endpoints.

findings.title: Many write and read endpoints declare no error responses
findings.location: PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; POST /developer/v1/cards/physical; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements/{reimbursement_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}
findings.evidence: PATCH physical card has only a 200 response. GET virtual card has only a 200 response. GET reimbursement and GET reimbursements have only 200. PATCH transaction has only 200. Some endpoints document 400 and others do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a documented 400/401/403/404 response using DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical 400 response is an untyped string
findings.evidence: "400": {"description":"Error", "content": {"application/json": {"schema": {"type":"string"}}}}
findings.suggested_fix: Return the DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema, as other endpoints do, so the error body is typed.

findings.title: Mileage POST and receipt upload use different auth and error patterns
findings.evidence: "security": [] (no auth) on a write endpoint while all other operations require oauth2 scopes; it documents only a 401 response.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override or explain it, and add the required reimbursements:write scope.

findings.title: Vault POST security scope differs from its sibling endpoints
findings.evidence: security: cards:read_vault and limits:write, while the GET /cards/vault/{card_id} uses only cards:read_vault. The operation both creates a limit and returns PAN/CVV.
findings.suggested_fix: Document why both scopes are needed and state in the description what sensitive data the response returns.

findings.title: Idempotency key is optional on create but not on receipt upload
findings.evidence: Vault POST has header X-Idempotency-Key with required: false. Receipt upload has body field idempotency_key listed in required, but the same concept is a header elsewhere. POST /cards/physical and POST /reimbursements/mileage have no idempotency key at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header or body) with consistent required status across all create endpoints.

findings.title: Receipt upload path and parameter names are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Path uses singular 'reimbursement' while other paths use 'reimbursements'. Body field 'reimbursee_id' is used here while the mileage body uses the same 'reimbursee_id', and list endpoints use 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the path to /reimbursements/submit-receipt and document how reimbursee_id differs from user_id.

findings.title: Transaction listing mixes casing in query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards uses 'userId' while every other filter uses snake_case 'user_id'. Transactions uses 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id and order_by_amount_asc, keeping snake_case throughout.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor and page_size limits are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Virtual cards: page_size has default 20 but no min/max constraint in schema. Reimbursements and transactions say 'must be between 2 and 100'. Physical cards list has no pagination parameters at all, yet returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same page_size and start parameters, with the same min/max constraints, to every paginated list endpoint.

findings.title: Physical card list endpoint has no paging parameters
findings.evidence: Operation id is 'get_physical_card_list_with_pagination' and the response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource, but parameters include only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters, or remove 'pagination' from the operation id and response if it is not paginated.

findings.title: Transaction list returns counts that the other lists lack
findings.evidence: Response is CountedPaginatedResponseApiTransactionCanonicalSchema with include_count described as 'total_count, capped at 10,000'. Other list endpoints return DeveloperAPINestedPage with no total_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the other list endpoints that total counts are unavailable, or add them consistently.

findings.title: Transaction amount field is deprecated but still typed as number
findings.evidence: Transaction: "amount": {"deprecated":true, "type":"number"}; SingleTransaction: "amount": {"deprecated":true, "type":"string"}. Same field, different types.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for amount in both schemas, or remove the field from SingleTransaction.

findings.title: Transaction SingleTransaction and Transaction amount/currency types conflict
findings.evidence: Transaction.original_transaction_amount uses CurrencyAmount (amount, currency_code), while merchant_amount uses ApiSignedAmount (currency, value). Both describe the same kind of money with different field names.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one money shape (for example ApiSignedAmount) across transaction and reimbursement schemas, or document the difference.

findings.title: Reimbursement schema marks many nullable fields as required with no nullability reason
findings.evidence: required includes 'payment_id', 'payment_batch_id', 'approved_at', 'distance', 'end_location', 'merchant' and 'employee_id', all declared nullable: true. Also 'waypoints' and 'trace_id' are not required in some places.
findings.suggested_fix: Document when each nullable required field is null, or make optional fields non-required.

findings.title: Card vault PAN and CVV returned with no declared protection
findings.evidence: CardDetails has pan: "Primary account number(PAN) of the card." and cvv: "Card verfication value." with no security note; GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id} declares only oauth2 cards:read_vault and no x-sensitive or equivalent marker. PhysicalCard.shipping.full_card_number is also a plain string.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark PAN/CVV as sensitive (e.g. x-sensitive: true, writeOnly/no-cache headers), document the protection, and add Cache-Control: no-store to the response.

findings.title: Full card number exposed in shipping object without protection
findings.evidence: "full_card_number":{"type":"string","description":"The full card number."} is part of CardShipping, returned by GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} (scope cards:read, not cards:read_vault).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from CardShipping or gate it behind cards:read_vault with the same sensitive-field marking as CardDetails.

findings.title: Card-creation and vault endpoints lack declared idempotency on writes
findings.evidence: POST /developer/v1/cards/vault defines optional header X-Idempotency-Key, but POST /developer/v1/cards/physical and POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage declare no idempotency mechanism; /reimbursement/submit-receipt uses a body field idempotency_key instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism (header, required on creates) consistently across all POST create endpoints.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security requirements
findings.evidence: "security":[] with no scope, and the only error response is 401; a creation endpoint that moves money has no declared oauth2 scope (reimbursements:write expected).
findings.suggested_fix: Declare security: [{oauth2: [reimbursements:write]}] matching the other reimbursement write endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card POST returns plain-string 400 error body
findings.evidence: "400":{"description":"Error","content":{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"string"}}}} whereas all other 400 responses use DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use $ref DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response and add x-trace-id header as elsewhere.

findings.title: Many error and success responses lack x-trace-id or error schema
findings.evidence: PATCH physical card declares only 200; GET virtual card only 200; GET vault card has 400 but PATCH transaction only 200; no DeveloperApiErrorResponse documented for these operations.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 400/401/404 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse and x-trace-id on every operation.

findings.title: Pagination parameter naming inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual (userId, start); GET /developer/v1/cards/physical (user_id); GET /developer/v1/transactions (orderByAmountAsc vs order_by_amount_desc)
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is "userId" while all others use "user_id"; transactions has "orderByAmountAsc" alongside snake_case "order_by_amount_desc" and "order_by_date_asc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to snake_case (user_id, order_by_amount_asc) and keep one convention for all query parameters.

findings.title: Pagination start cursor and page_size limits not enforced in schema
findings.evidence: page_size is "type":"integer","default":20 with description "must be between 2 and 100" but no minimum/maximum; start is an unconstrained string. Physical card list has no page_size or start parameter at all despite returning a paginated response.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2, maximum: 100 to page_size and add start/page_size to the physical card list, or document why not.

findings.title: Physical card list parameters conflict with description and naming
findings.evidence: Description says cards "can be filtered by ... display name" and the parameter is display_name, but include_activated_only says "Defaults to True if not specified" and no default is in schema; include_terminated_only defaults are only in prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Put defaults in the schema (default: true / false) so the type and description agree, and align filter names with the response field names.

findings.title: Transaction amount types conflict with description
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is "type":"number" (float) while SingleTransaction.amount is "type":"string", both marked deprecated; min_amount/max_amount accept decimal string or number via oneOf.
findings.suggested_fix: Make amount type consistent across Transaction and SingleTransaction and document precision; prefer string decimals or integer minor units throughout.

findings.title: Reimbursement state filter and transaction state enum inconsistent
findings.evidence: Transaction state enum includes "ALL" as a state value, which is a query sentinel not a valid stored state; the response schema for state therefore allows a value that never occurs.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove ALL from the response state enum and keep it only as a request filter value.

findings.title: Reimbursement user identifier named inconsistently
findings.evidence: Query param user_id has no description and is declared last among parameters; create body uses reimbursee_id for the same concept (POST /reimbursements/mileage and submit-receipt).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name for the reimbursement owner concept across list filters and create bodies, and describe user_id.

findings.title: Operation summary contradicts method for virtual card GET
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation, returning a VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and verify no delete operation was intended.

findings.title: Split transaction PATCH is destructive yet lacks safety docs
findings.evidence: Operation has "x-destructive":true and an empty line_items array 'unsplit (remove all line items)' but no idempotency or concurrency guidance, and tags include both "Transaction" and "transactions" (case-variant duplicate tag).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate 'transactions' tag and document the replace semantics and how to retry safely.

findings.title: Transaction amount fields lack unit and sign clarity
findings.evidence: "amount": {"deprecated": true, "description": "Deprecated. Use `entity_amount`.", "type": "number"} in Transaction, but typed as "type": "string" in SingleTransaction. Same field, different types across list and single endpoints; no unit stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one type (string decimal or number) for amount in both schemas and state the currency and unit explicitly, or remove the field before sunset.

findings.title: Currency amount units inconsistent across endpoints
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmount.amount: "expressed in cents"; ApiSignedAmount.value: "smallest denomination"; ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody.amount: "Amount in minor units (e.g. 5000 = $50.00)"; ApiSpendingRestrictionsRequestBody.limit: "denominated in the smallest currency unit"; transaction-level "amount" is a plain decimal number. Multiple money representations with no single rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one money type (integer minor units plus currency and minor_unit_conversion_rate) everywhere and document it once.

findings.title: Request money amounts have no range or minimum
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmountRequestBody: "amount": {"type": "integer"} with no minimum, and no note on whether negative or zero is allowed. ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody: "amount": {"type": "integer"} with no minimum. By contrast ApiReimbursementAmount.value has "minimum": 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare minimum (and whether negatives are valid) on every amount input, and state the maximum allowed.

findings.title: Currency code is free string despite enum elsewhere
findings.evidence: "currency_code": {"default": "USD", "description": "The type of currency, in ISO 4217 format. e.g. USD for US dollars", "type": "string"} with no enum, while ApiSignedAmount.currency and ApiReimbursementAmount.currency carry a full enum. Also CurrencyAmount requires minor_unit_conversion_rate but the request type does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same ISO 4217 enum to all currency fields and document which currencies are supported for limits.

findings.title: Timestamps without format on several fields
findings.evidence: Reimbursement examples use "created_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" (malformed, missing hour), and ApiTransactionPurchaseLodging.check_in is "type": "string" with no format; ApiTransactionPurchaseFlightData.departure_date is "type": "string", nullable, no format.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare format: date or date-time on every date field and fix the malformed example timestamps.

findings.title: Date filter formats and time zones undefined
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements params from_date, to_date, from_submitted_at, to_transaction_date; GET /developer/v1/transactions from_date, to_date
findings.evidence: Parameter "to_transaction_date" description is just "Data."; "from_transaction_date" says "after this date" with format date-time, while transactions "from_date" says "ISO8601 format" with no timezone rule. Inclusive vs exclusive boundaries are not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the time zone (UTC expected), inclusive/exclusive semantics, and replace "Data." with a real description.

findings.title: Enum for reimbursement state missing from transaction filters and pagination limits incomplete
findings.evidence: Reimbursement and transaction page_size: "The value must be between 2 and 100." but the schema is only "default": 20, "type": "integer" with no minimum or maximum. Virtual cards page_size has the same default with no bounds; its description is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2 and maximum: 100 to every page_size schema, and state behavior when out of range.

findings.title: Pagination cursor type and meaning unspecified
findings.evidence: "start": {"type": "string"} described as "The ID of the last entity of the previous page", yet GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual and physical list use a different scheme with no start parameter at all, and physical cards list has no page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the cursor's opaque nature, and add consistent pagination params (page_size, start) across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination controls
findings.evidence: Parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only, yet the response is a PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a next URL. No start or page_size is accepted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size with bounds, or document the fixed page size and how to reach later pages.

findings.title: Default for include_activated_only contradicts parameter semantics
findings.evidence: "Filter only for activated cards. Defaults to True if not specified" with no schema default; and include_terminated_only "Defaults to False" also undeclared in schema. Defaults live only in prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare default values in the schema so client generators and docs agree.

findings.title: Reimbursement sync and funding fields have undocumented enum values
findings.evidence: funding_source enum includes "RAMP_FUNDED" with description "RAMP_FUNDED does not confirm settlement", while trace_id is described as "may be a trace ID, IMAD number, or reference number" with descriptor/trace_id both nullable and no format, so consumers cannot parse it reliably.
findings.suggested_fix: Document which rails return which trace types and define nullability and format precisely.

findings.title: Reimbursement pagination uses undocumented user_id param and inconsistent naming
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements param user_id and userId on GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual
findings.evidence: Reimbursements has "user_id" with no description; virtual cards list uses "userId" (camelCase) while every other filter is snake_case, e.g. "entity_id" and "is_terminated".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and add descriptions to every query param.

findings.title: Trip and transaction state enums incomplete for state filter
findings.evidence: Filter enum includes "ALL" and "DECLINED" but Transaction.state enum is identical; the description says "If state is not set, all transactions except declined transactions will be returned" with no statement of what the response state value will be when declined.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether declined transactions can appear in responses and document the ALL value's semantics.

findings.title: Responses lack error schema on several endpoints and 201 vs 200 inconsistency
findings.evidence: get_physical_card_resource returns "201" for success, while the other GETs return 200. POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400 returns "type": "string" instead of DeveloperApiErrorResponse. Many operations (e.g. PATCH physical card, POST mileage) declare no 400/404 at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for GET, use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all 4xx, and document error codes for each operation.

findings.title: Idempotency key defined inconsistently across creation endpoints
findings.location: POST /developer/v1/cards/vault header X-Idempotency-Key vs POST /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt body idempotency_key
findings.evidence: Vault creation: header "X-Idempotency-Key", optional, maxLength 255. Receipt upload: body field "idempotency_key" is required with no length limit. Other creates (physical card POST, mileage POST) have no idempotency mechanism at all, and the physical card POST can create cards that cost money.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize one optional-or-required idempotency key mechanism with defined retention window across all POST endpoints, starting with card creation.

findings.title: Approval states and statuses lack meaning and next steps
findings.evidence: Enum values such as 'PENDING' ('Pending Review'), 'APPROVED' ('Approved'), 'AWAITING_PAYMENT' ('Awaiting Payment'), 'EXPORTED' ('Exported for payment'), 'INIT' ('Init') and 'DRAFT' ('Draft') have only short labels. Nothing says which states are final, which precede approval, or which can move back.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description for each state explaining whether it is pending, approved, paid, or terminal, and what transitions are possible.

findings.title: Transaction approval_status values are undefined
findings.evidence: Enum: AWAITING_EMPLOYEE, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_CHANGES_REQUESTED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_MISSING_ITEMS, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_REPAYMENT_FAILED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_REPAYMENT_REQUESTED, AWAITING_REVIEWER, FULLY_APPROVED. No descriptions are provided, and the Transaction schema has no approval_status field to confirm the values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add x-enum-descriptions for each value and include approval_status in the Transaction response schema with the same definitions.

findings.title: Transaction 'state' enum mixes states and filter values
findings.evidence: Response state enum includes 'ALL', which is described as 'Special filter value to include all transaction states'. The description for state says only 'transaction state.' It is unclear whether 'COMPLETION' or 'PENDING_INITIATION' is final.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'ALL' from the response schema enum and define the lifecycle order of the remaining states.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'sync_status' and 'synced_at' semantics unclear
findings.evidence: sync_status enum NOT_SYNC_READY/SYNCED/SYNC_READY has descriptions, but 'synced_at' says 'Time when reimbursement has been synced. Will be None if...' while the field is nullable and no timezone is given. The 'sync_status' field is marked readOnly with no description.
findings.suggested_fix: State who or what triggers sync, what 'NOT_SYNC_READY' requires, and whether synced_at is in UTC.

findings.title: Amount fields are inconsistent and some lack units
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is 'type: number' and deprecated, while SingleTransaction.amount is 'type: string' with the same description 'Deprecated. Use entity_amount.' Neither says what currency or units it uses. Transaction.entity_amount is an integer in minor units, while merchant_amount is also signed without explaining which amount is what the business is charged.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the type of 'amount' identical in both schemas, and state the currency and minor-unit meaning of each amount field.

findings.title: Negative and signed amounts not explained for approvals
findings.evidence: ApiSignedAmount.value: 'May be negative for refunds or credits.' Transaction.entity_amount is described as 'signed: refunds and credits can be negative.' No guidance is given on how a negative amount affects approval thresholds or totals.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain how negative amounts are treated for approval, reporting, and split totals.

findings.title: Transaction split behavior and line-item sums undefined
findings.evidence: Description says 'the line item amounts must sum to the transaction amount', but does not say which amount (entity_amount, merchant_amount, or amount) or what happens on a mismatch. Operation is marked 'x-destructive': true, yet the description does not say what is overwritten.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the exact amount field used for the sum, document the error on mismatch, and state what previous splits or memos are replaced.

findings.title: No audit trail or who/when fields on approvals
findings.evidence: Transaction has 'updated_at' described only as 'Approximate transaction updated timestamp... Computed as the latest of user transaction time, settlement time, and transaction interaction state update time.' Reimbursement has 'updated_at' with no description. No field identifies who approved, rejected, or last changed a record.
findings.suggested_fix: Add approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, and last_modified_by fields, or explain how these are retrieved, with the timestamp source documented.

findings.title: Reimbursement dates have undefined meaning
findings.evidence: Query 'from_date' is 'Filter reimbursements created after this date' while 'from_transaction_date' is 'Filter by underlying transaction date (after this date)'. 'to_transaction_date' has the description 'Data.' Reimbursement.transaction_date is a 'date' with no definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Data.' with a real definition and state whether date filters are inclusive, and which timezone applies.

findings.title: Transaction date filter descriptions conflict
findings.evidence: from_date: 'with a user_transaction_time after the given date'. order_by_date_asc: 'Sort transactions by user_transaction_date...' which is a field name that does not exist in the Transaction schema (the field is user_transaction_time). 'accounting_date' is described separately as based on cleared date or manual override.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent date field name, and state which date (user_transaction_time, settlement_date, or accounting_date) each filter uses.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'spend_limit_id' versus 'fund_id' is unclear
findings.evidence: spend_limit_id is 'deprecated: true', described as 'Alias of fund_id (Fund).' Mileage create uses 'spend_allocation_id' described as 'Unique identifier of the fund', and the list endpoint has no fund filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one name for the fund across request and response, and document the deprecation date and replacement.

findings.title: Physical card states and suspension reversibility unclear
findings.evidence: state enum: 'ACTIVE','CHIP_LOCKED','SUSPENDED','TERMINATED','UNACTIVATED'. Post suspension says 'The suspension is revertable.' but no reference to who may unsuspend. The DELETE for termination says only 'irreversible', and 'x-destructive' is absent from it.
findings.suggested_fix: State which actor can make each state change and what audit record is produced.

findings.title: Virtual card DELETE described as 'Permanently delete' but GET
findings.evidence: summary: 'Permanently delete this resource' on a GET operation, with a description of 'Get single virtual card'.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to describe fetching the card, and confirm whether any delete operation exists for virtual cards.

findings.title: Vault 'Create' response type mismatch
findings.evidence: Summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' returns schema PCILimit, which has 'restrictions' and 'card' but no description of whether the request's 'accounting_rules' were applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Document whether the returned limit reflects the accounting_rules sent, and what the 'allowed_overage_percent_override' null means.

findings.title: Transaction 'card_holder' and attendee fields need source
findings.evidence: card_holder is 'Information about the card holder' with department_name and location_name but no note that these are copied at transaction time or live values. attendees: 'List of attendees for the transaction' with user_id that may be null.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether card_holder values are snapshots at the time of the transaction and when attendee user_id is null.

findings.title: Scopes not declared for vault create endpoint's card reads
findings.evidence: security: [{"oauth2":["cards:read_vault","limits:write"]}] - the operation requires both scopes together, but the summary 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' does not say both are needed, and it is unclear whether a token with only one scope gets partial results or a 403.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the description that both cards:read_vault and limits:write are required (AND semantics), and document the 401/403 response for a missing scope.

findings.title: Auth-failure responses undocumented on most operations
findings.location: All operations except POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage and POST /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt
findings.evidence: Only POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage and submit-receipt document 401; e.g. GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id} lists only 200 and 400 while requiring oauth2 cards:read_vault, and POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage has "security": [] while declaring a 401 response.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare 401 and 403 consistently on every secured operation, and fix the mileage endpoint's empty security array so its auth requirement is explicit.

findings.title: Mileage create endpoint has empty security requirement
findings.evidence: "security":[],"summary":"Create a mileage reimbursement" - no scope is named, yet the same operation returns 401 Unauthorized.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to oauth2 with reimbursements:write, or explain why no scope is needed.

findings.title: Summary of virtual card GET says 'Permanently delete'
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation whose description is absent and whose response is "Get single virtual card".
findings.suggested_fix: Change the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and add a DELETE operation if deletion is intended.

findings.title: Physical card delete vs. terminate wording is ambiguous
findings.evidence: summary "Terminate a card", description "Please note that this action is irreversible."; the sibling POST /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}/suspension is described as "The suspension is revertable." and the unsuspend DELETE has no description.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent verbs and state explicitly in each description which action is reversible and which endpoint undoes it.

findings.title: Unsuspend and suspend operations use inconsistent verbs
findings.evidence: DELETE /suspension has summary "Unsuspend a card" with no description and no 400 response, while POST /suspension returns 400 and says "The suspension is revertable."
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description and 400 response to the DELETE, and make the suspend/unsuspend pair symmetric.

findings.title: Transaction list filters conflict with sync_status precedence
findings.evidence: sync_status: "If set, it supersedes sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits", while sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits remain separate parameters with no deprecation note.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark sync_ready and has_no_sync_commits deprecated, or document the precedence in a single place.

findings.title: Date filters for transactions use different fields
findings.evidence: from_date "Filter for transactions with a user_transaction_time after..." and order_by_date_asc "Sort transactions by user_transaction_date" (a field name not in the Transaction schema); updated_after is not documented as to which timestamp.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same field name everywhere (user_transaction_time) and state which timestamp updated_after compares against.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination and sort parameter naming
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is "userId" while all other filters are snake_case user_id; transactions sort uses "orderByAmountAsc" alongside "order_by_amount_desc" and "order_by_date_asc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId and orderByAmountAsc to snake_case and add the missing order_by_amount_asc counterpart.

findings.title: Reimbursement filter 'data' description is meaningless
findings.evidence: "description":"Data." for to_transaction_date; similarly include_merchant_data and GET /transactions/{transaction_id} include_merchant_data use "Data."
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the filter (e.g. 'Filter transactions dated before this timestamp') and state what extra data include_merchant_data adds.

findings.title: Pagination 'start' cursor semantics are unclear
findings.evidence: "start": "The ID of the last entity of the previous page..." with type string, while the response page.next is a full URL string with '<new_params>' placeholder; physical cards list has no start/page_size at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that the next URL should be used verbatim, and give physical card listing the same pagination parameters or state why it has none.

findings.title: Reimbursement submit-receipt idempotency is duplicated
findings.evidence: Request body has required "idempotency_key" while the vault creation endpoint uses header "X-Idempotency-Key" (optional); the receipt endpoint's 201 response does not say whether repeat calls return the same reimbursement.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism (header or body) across endpoints and document the replay behavior and response on a duplicate key.

findings.title: Receipt endpoint path differs from reimbursements resource
findings.evidence: Path uses singular "reimbursement/" while all other reimbursement paths use "reimbursements" (e.g. /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt, or keep the old path as a documented alias.

findings.title: Physical card POST response contract is unclear
findings.evidence: 400 response has "schema": {"type":"string"} while every other endpoint returns DeveloperApiErrorResponse; GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 201 instead of 200 for success.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 and return 200 for the GET success case.

findings.title: Transaction split fields reference unlisted ids and lookup keys
findings.evidence: Description says "Send line_items with amounts (in minor units)" but ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody.amount is an integer with no currency, and the transactions list returns entity_amount in value form; the patch 200 response does not define any error responses (no 400) despite the description requiring amounts to sum to the transaction amount.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 400 response with error codes for sum mismatch and document the currency of amount, and the required error response.

findings.title: No rate limit, retry, or backoff guidance anywhere in spec
findings.evidence: The spec has no description of rate limits, 429 responses, Retry-After headers, or retry guidance; no operation documents a 429 or 5xx response.
findings.suggested_fix: Document per-client rate limits, add 429 responses with Retry-After, and state which failures are safe to retry.

findings.title: Mutating POSTs lack idempotency keys
findings.evidence: Only POST /developer/v1/cards/vault defines X-Idempotency-Key as optional; create-physical-card and mileage-reimbursement have no idempotency input, and submit-receipt has a required idempotency_key in the body with no description of its retention window or conflict behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism consistently to all POST create operations and document key lifetime and replay behavior.

findings.title: Idempotency mechanism inconsistent between header and body
findings.evidence: Vault creation uses header 'X-Idempotency-Key' (optional, 1-255 chars), while receipt upload uses a required body field 'idempotency_key' with no length limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one transport (header) and one validation rule set for idempotency keys across all endpoints.

findings.title: Page size limits are documented inconsistently or missing
findings.evidence: Virtual cards, reimbursements, and transactions state 'must be between 2 and 100' for page_size, but physical cards list has no page_size or pagination parameters at all despite returning PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource.
findings.suggested_fix: Add page_size (min, max, default) and a cursor parameter to every paginated list, including physical cards.

findings.title: Pagination cursor semantics are unclear
findings.evidence: 'start' is described as 'The ID of the last entity of the previous page', typed as plain string, and page.next is a URL template '<resources>?<new_params>' with no example of a real next link.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to 'cursor' or document it as opaque, state whether next is absolute and how to detect the last page, and document ordering guarantees.

findings.title: Physical card list cannot be paginated or sorted
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource, yet the operation defines only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only with no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same start and page_size parameters used by the other list endpoints.

findings.title: Pagination and filter parameter names mix conventions
findings.evidence: Query params use camelCase 'userId' and 'orderByAmountAsc' alongside snake_case 'user_id', 'order_by_date_asc', and 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on snake_case for every query parameter and deprecate the camelCase names with an alias period.

findings.title: Inconsistent success status codes across operations
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 201; POST /developer/v1/cards/physical returns 200; DELETE /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} returns 204
findings.evidence: GET '/developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}' responses lists '201': Success; POST '/developer/v1/cards/physical' lists '200': Success for creation.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads, 201 for creates, and 204 or 200 consistently for deletes, correcting the GET 201 response.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented or untyped on many operations
findings.location: POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400; PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; POST /developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage 401 only
findings.evidence: POST /developer/v1/cards/physical 400 uses schema type 'string' rather than DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH and several GET list operations define no error responses; reimbursement list has no 400 despite filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all 4xx and 5xx responses and document the error_code values per operation.

findings.title: Error descriptions are vague and not operation-specific
findings.evidence: Responses say 'raises CardInvalidInput' or 'raises TransactionInvalidInput', which are implementation exception names rather than client-facing descriptions; error_code values are never enumerated.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with client-facing descriptions and list the stable error_code values each operation can return.

findings.title: Ambiguous mixed-state transaction list default
findings.evidence: Description says 'If state is not set, all transactions except declined transactions will be returned', while the 'state' enum includes 'ALL' and the note on 'include_count' says counts add latency; no default is in the schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the default in the schema and state explicitly how 'ALL' differs from the unset default.

findings.title: Unclear and deprecated amount fields in transaction schema
findings.evidence: 'amount' is 'type: number' in Transaction but 'type: string' in SingleTransaction, and is marked deprecated; 'limit_id' is deprecated but still required-adjacent with 'fund_id' returning the same value.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix one type for amount across both schemas and set a removal date for deprecated fields.

findings.title: Patch semantics for transaction split are unclear and destructive
findings.evidence: Marked 'x-destructive': true; description says 'Send an empty line_items array to unsplit' and line_items 'Omit to leave splits unchanged', with no statement on whether repeated calls are safe or what happens on partial failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Document replacement semantics, retry safety, and the conflict response when amounts do not sum to the transaction amount.
